name: Webhooks
summary: One private URL. A direct line to your phone.
description: Connect anything that can send an HTTPS POST request to a personal webhook in Nudge. Get a notification when work is done or something needs your attention.
requirements: A personal hook created in the app
A tool that can send HTTPS POST requests

steps.title: Create your personal hook
steps.body: In Nudge, open You → Personal hooks and create a hook. Give it a useful name, then copy its private URL.

steps.title: Keep the URL private
steps.body: Anyone with this URL can send to this hook. Save it as a secret in your tool, not in source code or a shared chat.

steps.title: Connect your tool
steps.body: Send a POST request to the URL with Content-Type: application/json and a message field. Personal hooks notify your own account and need no separate API token.

note: Notifications depend on connectivity, device permissions and Focus settings. Personal hooks send text messages to your account.

name: Python
summary: Let your script tell you when it’s finished.
description: Step away from a long-running script. Use Python’s built-in HTTP tools to notify yourself when a task completes.

steps.title: Create your personal hook
steps.body: In Nudge, open You → Personal hooks and create a hook. Give it a useful name, then copy its private URL.

steps.title: Keep the URL private
steps.body: Anyone with this URL can send to this hook. Save it as a secret in your tool, not in source code or a shared chat.

steps.title: Send after your task
steps.body: Run this snippet when your task finishes. Handle network errors in your workflow and avoid repeating requests whose outcome is uncertain.

code:
import json
import os
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

request = Request(
    os.environ["NUDGE_WEBHOOK_URL"],
    data=json.dumps({
        "message": "Your Python job is complete."
    }).encode("utf-8"),
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    method="POST",
)
with urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
    print(response.status)
note: This recipe uses the Python standard library. No separate Nudge SDK is required.

name: Shell & cURL
summary: A small command. A useful heads-up.
description: Add a personal notification to a shell script, scheduled job, or build workflow with a simple HTTPS request.

steps.title: Create your personal hook
steps.body: In Nudge, open You → Personal hooks and create a hook. Give it a useful name, then copy its private URL.

steps.title: Keep the URL private
steps.body: Anyone with this URL can send to this hook. Save it as a secret in your tool, not in source code or a shared chat.

steps.title: Add your notification
steps.body: Run the command at the point where a notification is useful. This example sends a fixed message without automatic retries.

code:
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 15 \
  --request POST "$NUDGE_WEBHOOK_URL" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"message":"Your build is ready to review."}'
examples: A scheduled command needs a check
note: This is a general HTTP recipe. Your runner must support outbound HTTPS.

name: JavaScript
summary: Turn a server-side event into a nudge.
description: Use fetch in a server-side JavaScript workflow to notify yourself about a useful event. Keep the webhook away from browser code.

steps.title: Create your personal hook
steps.body: In Nudge, open You → Personal hooks and create a hook. Give it a useful name, then copy its private URL.

steps.title: Keep the URL server-side
steps.body: Save it in your server’s secret environment. Never embed the URL in a public website or browser bundle.

steps.title: Send when it matters
steps.body: Call the webhook after the event you care about. An accepted request is not proof that a phone displayed the alert.

note: Personal hooks notify your own account. Register as a platform to send notifications to your product’s subscribers through the platform API.

name: Automations
summary: Your workflow runs. Your phone keeps you posted.
description: Connect a workflow tool that supports custom HTTP requests. Add a Nudge webhook step after the event you care about.
requirements: An automation tool with an HTTPS request action
A plan that allows custom HTTP requests

steps.title: Choose your trigger
steps.body: Start with an event your tool already supports: a task finishing, a row changing, or a scheduled check.

steps.title: Add an HTTP request
steps.body: Choose POST, paste your private webhook as the URL and set Content-Type to application/json.

steps.title: Write a useful message
steps.body: Send a JSON body with a message field. Keep the text brief and avoid sensitive customer or account information.

steps.title: Test once
steps.body: Trigger the workflow once and check your Nudge inbox. If it arrives silently, review your phone’s notification permissions.

examples: A scheduled check finds a change
note: This guide uses a generic HTTP action, not a native integration or partnership with a specific automation provider.

name: IoT & devices
summary: A little signal from the things around you.
description: Connect a device or home-automation hub that can make HTTPS requests, and turn useful events into personal notifications.
requirements: A device or trusted hub with HTTPS POST support

steps.title: Choose an event
steps.body: Pick a non-critical event, such as a print completing or a home routine finishing.

steps.title: Connect through your hub
steps.body: Configure your device or hub to POST to the private webhook using Content-Type: application/json and a message field.

steps.title: Set sensible limits
steps.body: Use a threshold or cooldown in your automation so repeated sensor changes do not overwhelm your notifications.

note: Compatibility depends on your device or hub. Nudge is not an emergency alarm or a substitute for a dedicated safety system.

name: ChatGPT
summary: Ask for a nudge when your task is done.
description: The Nudge plugin connects supported assistant tasks to your personal webhook. Request a completion notification or enable optional alerts for longer tasks.
requirements: Access to the Nudge plugin preview
A supported ChatGPT or Codex environment

steps.title: Get preview access
steps.body: The plugin is in preview. Contact Nudge support for availability. A public installation link is not available on this page yet.

steps.title: Connect and configure
steps.body: Once you have access, connect Nudge and save your webhook in Configuration. Do not paste the URL into a shared chat.

steps.title: Ask for an alert
steps.body: Select Nudge and ask your assistant to notify you when the task is done. Optional automatic alerts apply to eligible tasks lasting five minutes or more.

code: Review this work and nudge me when it’s ready.
note: Assistant notifications are best-effort and depend on the host running the tool. They may not arrive after interruption, app closure or network failure. Automatic alerts do not run for every task.
